title: Evens Before Odds
statement:
You get an array of non-negative integers nums. Rearrange it so that every even number comes before every odd number, and return the result.

The order inside the even group and inside the odd group does not matter. Any arrangement that keeps all the original values and puts the evens first is accepted.

examples.why: The three evens come first, then the two odds. [6, 4, 2, 9, 7] would also be accepted.
Zero is even, so it moves to the front.
Already split correctly: nothing has to move.

hints: You never need to compare two evens or two odds with each other. What is the only question you ask about each number?
Collecting evens and odds into two lists and joining them works. Can you do it inside the same array?
Keep a pointer w to where the next even should go. Scan with i; whenever nums[i] is even, swap it into position w and move w forward.

explain.intuition:
This is a partition, not a sort. Each number falls into one of two buckets, and the buckets just need to be side by side. A full sort by parity would work but does more than needed.

The in-place version keeps a write pointer w: everything before w is already even. As a read pointer i scans the array, each even number it finds is swapped down to w. The number pushed out of w is one the scan has already passed, so it is odd (or it is the same element), and it is fine for it to end up further right. It is the same move as the partition step in quicksort.
steps: For each index i from left to right: if nums[i] is even, swap nums[i] and nums[w], then increase w.
When the scan ends, positions 0 … w − 1 hold all the evens and the rest hold the odds.
pitfalls: Treating 0 as odd or skipping it. 0 % 2 === 0, so zero is even.
Two pointers from both ends that move without checking bounds, so they cross and swap a finished pair back.
Assuming the checker wants one exact order. Any order inside each group is accepted, so don't waste time sorting.

solutions.title: Two buckets
solutions.idea: Collect the evens, then the odds, and join them. Simple and stable, but uses a second array.

solutions.title: In-place write pointer
solutions.idea: Swap every even number found by the scan into the next free slot at the front.

followups: Keep the original relative order inside each group while still using O(1) extra space. What does that cost in time?
Put evens at even indexes and odds at odd indexes when the counts match.
